component: Outline (Node.js) email OTP sign-in and rate limiter
classes: What a limit is bound to
root_cause: The email OTP callback had no per-code attempt cap and relied on the rate limiter, whose key was `user:<id>` taken from a JWT cookie that `getJWTPayload` only decoded without verifying (or, with no cookie, the client IP, which a misconfigured proxy setup could take from an unvalidated `X-Forwarded-For`), so each request could present a new key with a fresh quota; the fix caps OTP attempts at 10 and keys the limiter on user ID plus IP.
audit_scope: server/middlewares, server/utils and the email sign-in route that serves `/auth/email.callback`
notes: OSV lists 24954204eac2447b648d4e56813f69205ee4b873 as the fix, but that commit is only the v1.6.0 version bump. The security changes are PR #11613 (limiter key becomes `user:<id>:<ip>`, files server/middlewares/rateLimiter.ts and its test, read) and PR #11623 (10-attempt cap per OTP, files not read), both merged 2026-03-02; their merge commits appear only as short hashes (f0a7ee6, 1d86a4a), so full hashes are not given. The path server/utils/jwt.ts comes from the advisory. The file path of the OTP route was not confirmed.

component: Argo CD API server local-user brute-force protection (Go)
classes: What a limit is bound to
root_cause: Failed-login counters were keyed by username but kept in an in-memory cache capped at 1000 entries that removed a random entry when full, so login failures for many other usernames could evict the admin account's counter and reset its lockout; the fix never evicts the admin or the current user and raises the cap to 10000.
notes: Commit title 'Merge pull request from GHSA-2vgg-9h6w-m454'; it adds `pickRandomNonAdminLoginFailure()` and changes only util/session/sessionmanager.go and its test. OSV lists five more fix commits (branch backports, not read). Fixed releases: v2.8.13, v2.9.9, v2.10.4. The fix only protects the admin entry; counters of other accounts can still be evicted.

root_cause: `ConnectionExists()` allowed a new FTP transfer to reuse a pooled connection without comparing `CURLOPT_FTP_ACCOUNT`, `CURLOPT_FTP_ALTERNATIVE_TO_USER`, `CURLOPT_USE_SSL` and `CURLOPT_FTP_SSL_CCC`, so a transfer could run on a connection set up with other credentials or security settings; the fix stores these options per connection and compares them before reuse.
audit_scope: lib/url.c, lib/ftp.c, lib/ftp.h, lib/setopt.c and lib/urldata.h
notes: Affected curl 7.13.0 to 7.88.1; fixed in 8.0.0. Fix commit title 'ftp: add more conditions for connection reuse'.

root_cause: The classic builder reused a cached image for a build step when its parent and container config compared equal, but the config comparison skipped several fields (among them `Healthcheck` and `OnBuild`), steps built `FROM scratch` matched any image without a parent, and candidates were not limited to locally built images, so a pulled image could stand in for an unrelated build step; the fix compares the missing fields, adds the platform, and only considers locally built images.
notes: 3e230cfd is the merge commit of the security fix; `^` means its first parent. Patched releases v25.0.2, v24.0.9, v23.0.10. Only builds with the classic builder are affected (BuildKit disabled with DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0, or the /build API).

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: With `UsingOVM`, l2geth kept ETH balances in the OVM_ETH contract's storage and redirected `SetBalance`, `AddBalance` and `SubBalance` there, but `StateDB.Suicide` zeroed the account object's own balance field directly, so `opSuicide` credited the beneficiary while the destroyed contract kept its OVM_ETH balance and ETH was duplicated; the fix calls the redirected `SubBalance` in `opSuicide` after a fork height.
notes: Reported by Jay Freeman (saurik) on 2022-02-02; fixed in l2geth 0.5.11. PR #2146 was titled 'maintenance: decrease geth diff' to hide the fix and also carries unrelated upstream-sync edits; 9ef215b8 is its merge commit. The fix activates through `IsSDUpdate` at Optimism mainnet block 3135900. The official Optimism disclosure on Medium returned HTTP 403; the root cause follows the reporter's write-up and the diff. Node code, not a contract, so `onchain` is null.

component: LND Lightning node, on-chain HTLC resolution (Go)
root_cause: When a channel's confirmed commitment lacked an outgoing HTLC that was still on another valid counterparty commitment, the channel arbitrator failed the matching incoming HTLC back upstream (and marked it failed) without checking whether its preimage was already known, so a node whose downstream had already claimed the HTLC also refunded the upstream; the fix skips failback when the preimage is available.
notes: No CVE. Affected LND 0.17.5 and below; fixed in 0.18.0. The fix was hidden in the commit 'contractcourt: specify deadline and budget for anchor output' (merged 2024-04-19); its diff adds `if preimageAvailable { continue }` in contractcourt/channel_arbitrator.go. The disclosure shows simplified pseudocode (`failBackMissingHtlcs`, `failBackHtlc`) and links the real logic at contractcourt/channel_arbitrator.go lines 2079-2151 and htlcswitch/switch.go lines 1822-1872 as of f4035ade05d0c44b441f2fe26af89584a76a55d6. A variant (force close with LND's own commitment) was fixed later in 0.19.0 and is not part of this sample.

component: DPDK vhost library, virtio-net dequeue path
root_cause: `copy_desc_to_mbuf()` assumed the guest's virtio-net header fits in at most two descriptor buffers, so with a header split across more buffers the remaining length `buf_avail` underflowed to nearly 4 GB and the host allocated mbufs until the pool was empty, blocking other guests; the fixes walk the header across any number of buffers and drop descriptor chains no longer than the header.
notes: Two main-branch commits: dc1516e2 'vhost: fix header spanned across more than two descriptors' and 71bd0cc5 'vhost: discard too small descriptor chains'; their relative order was not checked, but dc1516e2^ still has the two-descriptor assumption. The advisory names the function `copy_desc_to_mbuf()`; at the fix it is `desc_to_mbuf()`. Stable fixes: 21.11.2, 20.11.6, 19.11.13. The GitHub links are the official mirror of git.dpdk.org (which blocked automated reads). OSV's fix-commit list for this CVE points at unrelated release commits and should not be used.

root_cause: `update_into` obtained the output buffer with `ffi.from_buffer(buf)` without `require_writable=True`, so an immutable object such as `bytes` passed as the output buffer was written in place, changing data that Python treats as read-only and possibly shared; the fix requires a writable buffer.
notes: d6951dca is the backport commit on the 39.0.x branch ('changelog + security fix backport (#8231)', release 39.0.1, which also bumps the bundled OpenSSL); the main-branch commit was not located. Affected since update_into appeared in 1.8. The advisory calls it a soundness bug: it needs a caller to pass an immutable buffer, attacker data alone cannot trigger it.

id: AWS CDK bootstrap staging bucket takeover (2024)
root_cause: The bootstrap template's file-publishing role and the CDK CLI addressed the asset staging bucket only by its predictable global name `cdk-{qualifier}-assets-{account}-{region}`, with no condition on the account that owns the bucket, so after the bucket was deleted another account could create a bucket with that name and receive, and change, the assets and templates CDK deployed; the fix adds an `aws:ResourceAccount` condition to the role policy and bumps the bootstrap version to 21.
notes: Reported by Aqua on 2024-06-27; fix merged 2024-07-12 in CDK v2.149.0; affects v2.148.1 and earlier. Accounts must re-run `cdk bootstrap` to get the new role policy. No CVE or vendor advisory page was read; the root cause follows the Aqua write-up and the commit.

component: Model catalogs and code that load Hugging Face models by `Author/ModelName` (Google Vertex AI Model Garden, Azure AI Foundry, open-source code)
root_cause: Hugging Face returned a deleted account's namespace to the pool (and the redirect left by an ownership transfer stopped working once the old account was deleted), while model catalogs and code fetched models by `Author/ModelName` alone without pinning a revision or re-checking the author, so whoever registered the freed name supplied the model that was deployed.
audit_scope: Any code, catalog entry or configuration that loads hub models by name, for example `from_pretrained("Author/ModelName")` calls without `revision`
notes: Closed-source platforms: question-level test only. Unit 42 published on 2025-09-03; Google added daily scans for deleted authors; no single fix commit. Open-source repositories with hard-coded model names are affected the same way, but no single repository is the sample.

root_cause: `ModelBackend.authenticate()` already ran the password hasher for unknown users, but `verify_password()` returned early without hashing for users with an unusable password, so response time showed which usernames exist with an unusable password; the fix runs `make_password()` on a random string in that branch and for a missing password or unknown hasher.
notes: Commits: main 5d864585, 5.0 branch 07cefdee, 4.2 branch 156d3186 (a 5.1 branch commit f5d16483 also exists). Fixed in 5.0.7 and 4.2.14. The code change is in hashers.py; backends.py is listed because ModelBackend.authenticate is the entry point.

root_cause: `_gnutls_proc_rsa_psk_client_kx()` branched on whether PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption of the client's premaster secret succeeded (the `randomize_key` path), so malformed and well-formed ciphertexts took measurably different time; the plain-RSA key exchange had been made branch-free for CVE-2023-0361, but this sibling path had not; the fix always prepares a random fallback and uses the result without branching.
notes: Fix commit 'auth/rsa_psk: side-step potential side-channel' taken from the Upstream-Status line of the OpenEmbedded backport (https://www.mail-archive.com/openembedded-core@lists.openembedded.org/msg190032.html); the commit page itself was not read. Fixed in 3.8.2. The GnuTLS issue links the earlier plain-RSA report #1050 (CVE-2023-0361, commit 80a6ce8ddb02477cd724cd5b2944791aaddb702a). CVE-2024-0553 is a later incomplete-fix follow-up and is not part of this sample.

root_cause: When updating timestamp, snapshot and targets metadata, the client did not load the previously trusted versions (so the version baseline defaulted to 0) and marked timestamp and snapshot as trusted before checking the versions they list, so validly signed but older metadata was accepted and clients could be rolled back to older targets; the fix reloads trusted metadata verified by the latest root and rejects any version decrease.
notes: Affected v0.2.0; fixed in v0.3.0. ed6788e7 is 'Merge pull request from GHSA-66x3-6cw3-v5gj'; it touches client/client.go, client/errors.go, verify/verify.go, verify/errors.go, util/util.go and two cmd/tuf-client files.

component: Strapi admin and users-permissions authentication (refresh-token sessions)
root_cause: On password change and reset, the admin and users-permissions controllers revoked refresh-token sessions only for a caller-supplied `deviceId`, and when it was omitted (the usual case) nothing was revoked, so refresh tokens issued before the change kept minting access tokens for up to 30 days; the fix revokes all of the user's refresh sessions unconditionally.
notes: Affected @strapi/admin and @strapi/plugin-users-permissions up to 5.33.2; fixed in 5.33.3. The advisory lists no commit; 64a197a8 is the commit of PR #25168 ('fix(users-permissions): implement session revocation on password changes'), whose diff changes both controllers listed in paths. `changePassword` and `resetPassword` are the users-permissions handlers named in the commit's tests; the admin handler name was not confirmed.
